To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found that the statistical model describes the light charged particle spectra in the fusion-evaporation exit channel, while the fusion-fission channel is dominated by pre-equilibrium emissions.

the 48 Ti on Ca 40 reaction at 300 and at 600 MeV is dominated by the fusion-evaporation channel and the fusion-fission channel is negligible; the statistical model is able to reproduce the experimental data; pre-equilibrium emissions are not observed in the energy spectra of the light charged particles; the statistical model parameters are not affected by the increase of the bombarding energy; the shape transitions can be observed in the high energy gamma ray emission gated on the evaporation residues and
we have measured the light charged particles in different mass channels and compared to the results of the statistical model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the 48 Ti + 40 Ca reactions at 300 and at 600 MeV in order to measure energy spectra and multiplicities for light charged particles in coincidence with the evaporation residues and to study the influence of the evaporation residues angular distribution on the shape of the GDR gamma rays.
the study of the decay of medium-mass compound nuclei in the mass region A = 100.
the study of fusion-evaporation and fusion-fission processes at energies around the barrier and the investigation of the onset of pre-equilibrium processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the 48 Ti on Ca 40 reactions, the statistical model is able to reproduce the experimental spectra and multiplicities for the light charged particles emitted in the FE and FF channels.

the statistical model, as implemented in the GEMINI code, describes well the data in terms of multiplicities and energy spectra of emitted charged particles, but it fails in reproducing the angular distributions.

- the FF channel is the dominant one for 300 MeV bombarding energies, - the FE channel is the dominant for 600 MeV, - the pre-equilibrium process is negligible at 300 MeV, - at 600 MeV the pre-equilibrium contribution is not negligible and it is not easy to be separated from the statistical model contribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FF process is the dominant one in this energy range.
the FF process dominates at 300 MeV, the FE process is the dominant one at 600 MeV and that the pre-equilibrium emission is negligible in the whole energy range.
the statistical model is in good agreement with the data, but the pre-equilibrium emission has to be considered in order to reproduce the data in the 600 MeV channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FF channel is the most important one in the 48 Ti on Ca40 reactions at 300 MeV, while it becomes less important when the bombarding energy is increased to 600 MeVs.
, at 600 MeV, the FF process is dominant with respect to the FE process.

the statistical model is in agreement with the experimental data and the shape transitions are not observed in the measured energy spectra and multiplicities for the emitted light charged particle in the decay of the excited compound nuclei.
